title: Evaluation and Management of Chest Pain in the Emergency Department
summary: A concise, evidence-based framework for rapid assessment, risk stratification, diagnostic pathways, and initial management of chest pain in the ED with emphasis on acute coronary syndrome, high-sensitivity troponin algorithms, and safe disposition.
clinicalQuestion: How should clinicians in the ED evaluate, risk stratify, and manage adults presenting with nontraumatic chest pain, with specific emphasis on suspected acute coronary syndrome?

keyMoments.title: Immediate Triage and ECG
keyMoments.body: Obtain ECG within 10 minutes; treat life threats. STEMI triggers emergent reperfusion.

keyMoments.title: High-Sensitivity Troponin Strategy
keyMoments.body: Use validated 0/1-h or 0/2-h algorithms; integrate absolute delta changes with clinical risk.

keyMoments.title: Structured Risk Assessment
keyMoments.body: Use HEART or EDACS with hs-cTn to guide disposition; aim for <1% 30-day MACE in discharge cohort.

keyMoments.title: Safe Disposition
keyMoments.body: Discharge low-risk with rapid follow-up; admit or observe intermediate-risk; activate cath for STEMI/high-risk NSTEMI.

keyMoments.title: Pathways and Chest Pain Centers
keyMoments.body: Standardized ED pathways and dedicated chest pain centers improve accuracy, speed, and resource use.

sections.title: Stepwise ED Approach to Chest Pain
sections.blurb: A prioritized sequence from triage to disposition built on contemporary guidelines and consensus.

steps.title: Primary Survey and Immediate Actions
steps.body: Assess airway, breathing, circulation; place on monitor, obtain IV access, pulse oximetry. Obtain 12‑lead ECG within 10 minutes. Treat hypoxemia, severe hypertension, and arrhythmias. If **STEMI is present**, activate reperfusion pathway immediately [1].

steps.title: Focused History and Risk Flags
steps.body: Characterize pain (onset, exertional, pressure-like), associated symptoms (dyspnea, diaphoresis, syncope), risk factors (CAD, diabetes, CKD), and red flags (hemodynamic instability, new HF, ongoing ischemia). Consider important differentials: PE, aortic syndromes, pericarditis, pneumothorax, esophageal rupture [6].

steps.title: Initial Diagnostics
steps.body: Obtain hs-cTn at presentation with repeat per validated algorithm (0/1‑h or 0/2‑h), BMP, CBC if indicated. Chest radiograph for alternative diagnoses. Serial ECGs if ongoing pain or dynamic symptoms. Use **hs‑cTn** thresholds and absolute deltas to adjudicate MI per guideline-aligned pathways [6], [8].

steps.title: Risk Stratification and Pathway Selection
steps.body: Combine clinical impression with a structured score (e.g., **HEART** or **EDACS**) plus hs‑cTn trajectory to classify as low, intermediate, or high risk for 30‑day MACE. Low-risk patients with negative hs‑cTn and nonischemic ECG are candidates for ED discharge with expedited follow-up [3], [6], [8].

steps.title: Treatment Aligned to Risk/Diagnosis
steps.body: Provide analgesia, nitrates if ischemic pain and not hypotensive, and antiplatelet therapy when ACS is likely. STEMI: immediate reperfusion. NSTEMI/Unstable angina: antithrombotics and early cardiology evaluation; consider invasive strategy by risk profile [1], [6].

steps.title: Disposition and Follow-up
steps.body: Low risk: discharge with clear return precautions and rapid outpatient testing if indicated. Intermediate risk: ED observation with repeat hs‑cTn, ECGs, and possible noninvasive testing. High risk or diagnostic uncertainty: admit. Use chest pain center protocols to optimize throughput and outcomes [2], [7].

sections.title: Key Checklists and Algorithms
sections.blurb: Operational elements that standardize care and reduce missed ACS.

cards.title: Time Targets
items: ECG completed and interpreted: ≤10 minutes
Repeat ECG: for persistent/recurring pain or dynamic changes
hs‑cTn repeat draw: 1 hour (preferred) or 2 hours per assay validation

cards.title: hs‑cTn Algorithms
items: 0/1‑h: baseline and 1‑h hs‑cTn; use assay‑specific rule‑out/rule‑in cutoffs and absolute delta
0/2‑h: alternative when 1‑h logistics limited
Single‑sample rule‑out possible if symptom onset >3 h and very low hs‑cTn, nonischemic ECG, low clinical risk [6], [8]

cards.title: Risk Scores (with hs‑cTn)
items: HEART score: history, ECG, age, risk factors, troponin
EDACS: symptom characteristics + risk factors + age
Use scores to guide disposition; target **<1% 30‑day MACE** for discharge cohorts [3], [6]

cards.title: Red Flags for Immediate Action
items: ST‑elevation or new LBBB with ischemic symptoms
Hypotension, shock, new/worsening heart failure
Refractory chest pain or dynamic ST‑T changes
Concern for aortic dissection, PE, tamponade, tension pneumothorax

cards.title: ACS Initial Therapies
items: Aspirin loading if no contraindication
Nitrates for pain/ischemia; avoid if hypotension, RV infarct, or PDE‑5 inhibitors
Anticoagulation for NSTEMI/UA when diagnosis likely
High‑intensity statin initiation for confirmed ACS
Beta‑blocker if no contraindications; defer in shock/acute HF

cards.title: Disposition Guide
items: Low risk + negative hs‑cTn algorithm + nonischemic ECG: discharge with expedited follow‑up
Intermediate risk: observation, serial hs‑cTn/ECG ± functional or anatomic testing
High risk or positive algorithm: admit; STEMI/NSTEMI pathways

sections.title: What the Evidence Supports
sections.blurb: Synthesis of high‑impact findings informing ED chest pain care.

steps.title: Guideline Consensus
steps.body: Recent multisociety guidance endorses **hs‑cTn‑based accelerated diagnostic pathways** with early ECG and structured risk assessment to safely increase ED discharges while maintaining low 30‑day MACE rates [6].

steps.title: High‑STEACS and Rapid Rule‑Out
steps.body: Implementation of **hs‑cTnI** with low thresholds enables **rapid rule‑out within 1 hour** for many patients, reducing admissions without increasing adverse events; these strategies underpin modern ED pathways [8].

steps.title: Chest Pain Centers and Pathways
steps.body: **Dedicated chest pain centers** and standardized protocols improve diagnostic speed, accuracy, and cost‑effectiveness compared with ad hoc care, supporting system‑level adoption [2], [7].

steps.title: Focused ACS Risk Stratification
steps.body: Combining clinical scores (e.g., **HEART/EDACS**) with hs‑cTn trajectories improves identification of low‑risk cohorts suitable for discharge, aiming for **<1%** short‑term MACE, aligning with guideline thresholds [3], [6].
